title: Tanzanian Coconut Fish Curry
community: Swahili coast — the everyday coastal fish dish
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Samaki wa Nazi — Tanzanian fish in coconut curry sauce. Fresh fish simmered gently in a rich coconut milk and tomato sauce fragrant with Zanzibar spices and coriander. The everyday fish dish of the Tanzanian coast.
longDesc: Samaki wa Nazi is the most widely eaten fish preparation on the Tanzanian coast — simple, fast, and extraordinary when made with the day's freshest catch. The coconut milk sauce brings the entire coastal flavour profile to the fish without masking its natural quality.
ingredients: 800g firm fish fillets — snapper, tilapia, or kingfish
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric. Set aside 10 minutes.
Cook onions until deeply golden. Add garlic, ginger, chillies.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, paprika. Cook 8 minutes until thick.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to gentle simmer.
Add fish. Spoon sauce over each piece.
Cover and simmer gently 10—14 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Add lemon juice. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Do not move fish until nearly cooked.
cookingScience: Fish proteins denature at 60—65°C. The gentle coconut milk simmer maintains temperatures at exactly this threshold — producing perfectly moist, just-flaking fish.
sustainabilityTips: Buy from local Zanzibar or coastal Tanzanian fishermen.
culturalNote: Samaki wa Nazi is the daily fish dish of the Tanzanian coast — the smell of coconut and spiced fish simmering is the afternoon smell of every coastal kitchen.
